datum.where: centre of the case outline in plan
datum.how_to_find_it: the band outer (95.6 x 111.4) and the tray outline (84.3 x 100.1) are both centred on it — measure the finished case, no source read needed

mating_plane.what: tray bottom = band bottom, coplanar and flat
mating_plane.rule: all base material at or below this plane

orientation.far_edge: y = 0, the USB / control-band edge, away from the user
orientation.landmark: the USB port is on the FAR edge
orientation.symmetry: the peg pattern is 4-fold symmetric — a base mounts in any of four 90 deg orientations

features.mouth_chamfer_note: MEASURED, not nominal. EFC_CHAMFER is 0.4 but OCCT refuses 0.4 and 0.3 on the tray's bottom face and _safe_chamfer settles at 0.2. Design the peg against 0.2.

peg.rule: the tray side is CAD-nominal and carries NO allowance; all fit lives on the peg
peg.gauge: print base_fit_gauge.stl, push each peg into any pocket, keep the rung that holds. Marks are raised dots: n dots = rung n, smallest first.

load_rating.path: vertical load goes through the FLAT MATING PLANE, never through the pegs. The pegs locate and resist shear.
load_rating.note: at even 30 MPa bearing that is ~250 N per peg against single-digit-newton service loads, so engagement depth is not the limiting factor — location is the job.

service_slots.what: BOOT / RESET tact access, pierced through the tray floor
service_slots.rule: any base covering this area MUST carry a through window; a base that stays inside Ø78.4 about the datum never reaches it

usb.rule: the USB face is on the FAR edge above the mating plane; a wedge that raises the far edge reduces plug clearance to the desk

stability.method: see agentpad13_base.py section 4 — CoP walk for vertical press, tip-vs-slide for horizontal push
stability.governing_case: firm press on the encoder knob edge, 56.1 mm from the datum
stability.ruling: A free-standing base smaller than the footprint must carry the mass itself. A Ø78 pedestal needs 52 g, which a SOLID print in PLA/PETG does reach — so v2.16 deletes the ballast and publishes an infill requirement instead. At 62% effective solidity (3 walls / 20% gyroid) it clears the 3 N design case but NOT the 5 N abuse case.

assumptions: Kailh BOX Jade 1.9 g — NO published mass exists; +/-25% is +/-3 g across 13 switches
EC11 push force 2-4 N class -> 3.0 N design / 5.0 N abuse. This is the GOVERNING input and it is an ESTIMATE
keyswitch press 1.5 N design / 3.0 N abuse
mu = 0.4 bare printed plastic on desk, 1.2 TPU on desk (v2.15: feet deleted, so no rubber contact is assumed)
printed-part fill fractions are stated per row in mass_model
stability.resolved_2026_08_20: The long-standing 3M SJ61A1 dimension conflict (Ø7.92 x 5.08 per DigiKey/3M vs Ø7.9 x 2.2 as modelled) is MOOT for bases: v2.15 deletes every foot recess, so no base geometry, stance figure or desk plane in this module depends on a bumpon dimension any more. Feet are unofficial.

print.orientation: desk face on the bed, every variant
print.pedestal_infill: PRINT SOLID. The pedestal carries no ballast in v2.16 — its own printed mass is what keeps the device upright, so infill is a STRUCTURAL setting here, not a speed/cost one. A solid print clears the 5 N abuse case; a normal 3-wall / 20 % gyroid print (62% effective solidity) clears the 3 N design case but NOT abuse.
print.riser_material: TPU for a grip base, PETG/PLA for a rigid stand — same file either way
print.ballast: none — deleted in v2.16 (owner: "No need for the ballast if the diameter is reasonable enough")
